Automated CD architecture

The GitHub-hosted coordinator architecture for Project #3 task selection, isolated implementation, evidence, review, QA, guarded merge and encrypted recovery state.

DeveloperOperatorArchitectEvaluatorReferenceINTERNAL
PrerequisitesA checkout of the CALIBER repository · Access to GitHub Actions and Project #3 for operational changes
Reviewed 2026-11-06 · Current CALIBER automated-cd implementation; budget contract follows PR #1204

Automated CD is CALIBER's GitHub-hosted software-engineering coordinator. It turns a Ready child Task in GitHub Project #3 into an isolated implementation, local evidence, a reviewable pull request, required CI checks, and—when the repository policy allows it—a verified merge and Project Done transition. The workflow is a delivery control plane, not a local cron job, product runtime, or replacement for the GitHub Project.

At a glance#

ConcernCurrent design
Canonical backlogGitHub Project #3 items and linked issue contracts
Execution unitAn open issue represented as Item type=Task, never an Epic or Gate
TriggerGitHub Actions schedule at 04:00 in America/Los_Angeles, or manual workflow_dispatch
Daily completion targetSix merged, closed, Project Done Tasks; attempts and opened PRs do not count
Daily model budget$30.00 across planner, developer, reviewer, and QA calls for one Pacific calendar day
Isolation boundaryA hosted runner, a temporary linked worktree, and an unprivileged worker user
Review boundaryDeterministic coordinator checks plus model review and QA; GitHub branch protection remains authoritative
Durable evidenceEncrypted SQLite state artifact, bounded usage report, PR/CI evidence, and GitHub audit history

Signature architecture#

flowchart LR
    Schedule["GitHub Actions schedule<br/>04:00 America/Los_Angeles"]:::async --> Runner["Hosted runner"]:::async
    Dispatch["Manual workflow_dispatch"]:::user --> Runner
    Runner --> Preflight["Validate inputs, secrets and token scope"]:::ctrl
    Preflight --> Restore["Restore encrypted workflow state"]:::store
    Restore --> Snapshot["Read Project #3 and repository overview"]:::ctrl
    Snapshot --> Planner["Deterministic eligibility and conflict planner"]:::ctrl
    Planner --> Claim["Claim Task and create linked worktree"]:::ctrl
    Claim --> Roles["Bounded Claude roles"]:::ext
    Roles --> QA["Local checks, coverage and QA verdict"]:::ctrl
    QA --> PR["Open PR with evidence"]:::ctrl
    PR --> Gates["Exact-head CI, reviews and mergeability"]:::async
    Gates -->|all required gates pass| Merge["Guarded GitHub merge"]:::ctrl
    Gates -->|failure or ambiguity| Block["Block Task and retain audit state"]:::ctrl
    Merge --> Reconcile["Verify main, close issue, set Project Done"]:::ctrl
    Reconcile --> Seal["Encrypt and upload state artifact"]:::store
    Block --> Seal
Actor UI / SPA Control plane Storage External Async worker

The coordinator is deliberately split into two trust domains:

  1. GitHub Actions and the Python coordinator may use Git, GitHub, Project, and private state credentials.
  2. Claude roles and local QA run without those credentials. The model receives only the tools and working directory required for its role.
Deep reference · data models, APIs & lifecycle

Reference#

System boundaries and authorities#

BoundaryAuthority or responsibility
GitHub Project #3Backlog, item type, status, readiness, release, priority, human-input phase, dependencies and ownership
Linked issueObjective, acceptance criteria, files, prerequisites, tests, failure oracle and documentation contract
.agents frameworkTransition semantics, engineering policy, project integration and repository review rules
GitHub ActionsHosted trigger, secret injection, runner lifecycle, concurrency and artifact retention
Python coordinatorEligibility, claims, worktree lifecycle, model-role sequencing, evidence capture, PR and merge orchestration
Claude CodeBounded planning, implementation, review and QA reasoning inside the supplied worktree
GitHub branch protectionRequired checks, independent approvals, mergeability and final remote enforcement
SQLite state artifactExecution evidence and recovery state; it is not a second backlog or source of task truth

The hierarchy is intentional: an Epic explains a package of work, while a child Task is the executable unit. Gates and controls express acceptance or release decisions and must not be selected as feature work. A child Task is not eligible merely because its parent Epic is Ready.

Hosted trigger and runner lifecycle#

sequenceDiagram
    participant GH as GitHub Actions
    participant R as Runner
    participant C as Coordinator
    participant P as Project #3
    participant A as Artifact store

    GH->>R: Start scheduled or manual workflow
    R->>R: Checkout main and install Python and Claude Code
    R->>R: Validate dispatch inputs and required secrets
    R->>A: Download latest encrypted state artifact
    A-->>R: workflow.state.enc or first-run empty state
    R->>P: Verify scoped token, repository permission and Project access
    R->>C: Run hosted coordinator
    C->>P: Snapshot items, issues, dependencies, PRs and branches
    C->>C: Plan, claim, execute and monitor
    C->>A: Seal SQLite state after execution
    R->>GH: Publish bounded progress, usage and failure status

The workflow is GitHub-only. No local scheduler is installed or required. GitHub's timezone-aware schedule follows Pacific daylight and standard time; GitHub can delay a scheduled start during periods of Actions load. The workflow concurrency group prevents overlapping hosted executions, while the local SQLite lock protects the restored state within one runner.

StageMain actionFailure behavior
InitializeCreate a mode-700 state directory and SQLite slotStop before checkout or model work

Project verificationConfirm token scopes, repository push permission, owner identity and open Project #3Stop before planning if Project access is incomplete
Worker isolationCreate autocdqa, temporary worktrees and credential-free QA environmentStop if the worker can read coordinator state

Configuration contract#

The authoritative defaults are in automated-cd/config/workflow.toml. Environment variables may override them on the hosted runner, but the checked-in file is the reviewable baseline.

SettingCurrent valueMeaning
daily_time04:00Local start threshold used by the coordinator
timezoneAmerica/Los_AngelesPacific calendar for schedule and daily accounting
project_view_number0All Project #3 items rather than one release view
daily_done_target6Merged, closed, Project Done Tasks counted for the day
max_tasks_per_run6Maximum new attempts across scheduled and manual runs for the day
max_workers2Maximum task workers; shared mutations remain serialized
auto_mergetrueAllows guarded merge only after all required gates pass
max_review_cycles3Developer-review-QA correction budget before blocking
daily_budget_usd30.0Aggregate Claude budget across one Pacific calendar day
max_budget_usd0.0Optional per-call cap; zero delegates the limit to remaining daily budget
agent_timeout_seconds3600Maximum wall time for one model role
stall_seconds900Maximum model silence before the role is considered stalled
qa_command_timeout_seconds7200Maximum time for one local QA command
ci_timeout_seconds43200Maximum PR-check wait before blocking
allow_overlapping_runsfalseKeep hosted runs and state writers serialized

Daily budget enforcement#

The $30 value is an aggregate budget, not a misleading per-call allowance. Before each planner, developer, reviewer or QA call, the coordinator:

  1. reads agent_started and agent_usage events since Pacific midnight;
  2. verifies every prior call has a finite, non-negative total_cost_usd result;
  3. computes the remaining amount;
  4. serializes the next model call under a process lock; and
  5. passes the smaller of the remaining daily amount and the optional per-call override to Claude Code's --max-budget-usd flag.

If a previous call has no trustworthy cost, or the remaining amount is zero, the coordinator stops safely rather than risk an unbounded or unmeasured run. The usage report still distinguishes the model's reported estimate from an invoice charge.

Project-driven planning#

flowchart TD
    Items["Project #3 snapshot"]:::store --> Open["Open issue and Project item"]:::ctrl
    Open --> Task["Item type = Task"]:::ctrl
    Task --> Todo["Status = Todo"]:::ctrl
    Todo --> Ready["Readiness = Ready"]:::ctrl
    Ready --> Human["Human input is None pending or acceptance-only"]:::ctrl
    Human --> Dependencies["Native blockers are closed and completed"]:::ctrl
    Dependencies --> Ownership["No assignee, open PR or prior same-day attempt"]:::ctrl
    Ownership --> Target["Release or milestone target resolves"]:::ctrl
    Target --> Paths["Reviewed path ownership determines parallelism"]:::ctrl
    Paths --> Eligible["Deterministic eligible set"]:::ctrl
    Eligible --> Model["Planner selects only from that set"]:::ext

The deterministic filter is evaluated before Claude sees a planning prompt. It requires all of the following:

Eligibility checkWhy it exists
Repository and Project item matchPrevent cross-repository or stale-view work
Issue is openClosed or historical work is never reopened by selection
Status=Todo and Readiness=ReadyRequire an explicit execution decision
Item type=TaskExclude Epics, Gates, Controls and Historical items
Human input is resolvedDo not invent a product decision; acceptance-only phases may proceed when safe
Native blockedBy dependencies are completedPreserve the issue DAG rather than guessing ordering
No assignee and no open PRAvoid taking work already owned or published
Release or milestone target resolvesKeep accounting and branch intent auditable
Allowlist and scope label matchRespect configured release or issue restrictions
Path conflicts are disjointPermit only reviewed parallel edits

The planner may narrow the deterministic set, but it cannot add an issue, override a blocker, make a Gate executable, or manufacture a human approval. Tasks without reviewed path ownership are treated as conflicting and therefore run serially with other substantial work.

Task state machine#

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> claimed
    claimed --> developing
    developing --> reviewing
    reviewing --> developing: findings or handoff gap
    reviewing --> qa: review approved
    qa --> developing: QA gap or command failure
    qa --> pr_open: QA approved
    pr_open --> ci_wait
    ci_wait --> ready: exact-head checks and reviews pass
    ci_wait --> blocked: failed, skipped, stale or timed-out gate
    ready --> merged_unreconciled: guarded merge returns
    merged_unreconciled --> done: main, issue and Project all verify
    claimed --> blocked: claim or setup ambiguity
    developing --> blocked: timeout, stall or unsafe mutation
    reviewing --> blocked: review-cycle limit
    qa --> blocked: QA-cycle limit
    blocked --> [*]
    done --> [*]

Every phase transition creates an append-only event. Recovery is deliberately asymmetric:

Phase at interruptionSafe automatic action
ci_wait, ready, merged_unreconciled with a PRRecheck exact head, required checks, reviews, mergeability and base
Before PR publicationMark the task Blocked and require branch, worktree and Project reconciliation
During GitHub mutationDo not replay; inspect the remote effect first
Blocked pre-PR taskRetry only after an owner-authored Ready transition, no remote branch or PR, and a fresh Ready claim

Bounded model roles#

RoleToolsResponsibilitiesForbidden authority
PlannerRead-only file toolsExplain the deterministic selection and narrow the batchCannot add tasks, claim Project items or mutate Git
DeveloperRead, Glob, Grep, Edit, WriteImplement the complete issue contract in its worktreeCannot access GitHub credentials, merge or modify main
ReviewerRead-only file toolsInspect the full candidate diff, task contract, checks and generated-artifact evidenceCannot edit, approve a GitHub review or merge
QARead-only file toolsVerify acceptance and test evidence after the reviewer approvesCannot edit, claim or merge

The trusted role policy is prepended to every prompt. Issue text, log text, review findings and tool output are untrusted data and cannot override the role policy. The coordinator validates JSON result schemas before acting on them.

Implementation and QA path#

flowchart LR
    Contract["Issue contract and Project fields"]:::store --> Worktree["Linked worktree from origin/main"]:::ctrl
    Worktree --> Setup["Seed Python 3.11 environment"]:::async
    Setup --> Develop["Developer edits isolated worktree"]:::ext
    Develop --> Diff["Candidate diff and ownership validation"]:::ctrl
    Diff --> Checks["Base, issue-specific and coverage checks"]:::async
    Checks --> Review["Reviewer sees diff and evidence"]:::ext
    Review -->|findings| Develop
    Review -->|approved| QA["QA verdict"]:::ext
    QA -->|gaps| Develop
    QA -->|approved| Publish["Coordinator commits, pushes and opens PR"]:::ctrl
    Publish --> Required["Required remote checks and review threads"]:::async
    Required --> Merge["Match-head guarded merge"]:::ctrl

The local gate includes git diff --check, docs validation, lint, type-check and backend smoke tests. Changed production Python also receives a full backend coverage run unless an issue-specific coverage command is configured. A command that exits zero after emitting SKIP is treated as not executed. Unsupported component changes such as UI, SDK, shell or configuration edits require explicit issue-specific commands.

Before a PR is published, the coordinator verifies that QA did not mutate the candidate. It compares the changed-file list and complete binary diff before and after review. Generated docs are synchronized from canonical sources and are included in the candidate. Large generated patches are summarized to the reviewer with exact paths, sizes and SHA-256 hashes, while staging still checks the complete patch.

GitHub and Project mutation sequence#

OperationMechanismVerification
Claim.agents/bin/engineering.mjs transition ... claim dry run, then applyRe-read Project and require Readiness=In Progress
Branchgit worktree add -b ... origin/mainBranch and worktree are coordinator-owned and isolated
PRCoordinator commits reviewed patch and creates a draft PRRecord PR number and exact head SHA
Review requestRequest Copilot when available and record reviewer statusNever represent self-review as independent approval
Remote gatePoll required checks, review decision, unresolved threads, mergeability and basePending, skipped, stale or failing is not pass
Mergegh pr merge --squash --match-head-commit, never admin bypassRe-read merge commit on main
CompletionClose issue as Completed and transition Project fields to DoneVerify issue state, merge evidence and Project snapshot

The coordinator does not push main directly. If main advances beyond the reviewed PR head, the candidate is stale and waits for a fresh implementation, review and QA cycle.

State, artifacts and observability#

flowchart TD
    SQLite["workflow.sqlite3<br/>runs, tasks, events"]:::store --> Seal["AES-GCM seal with AUTOCD_STATE_KEY"]:::ctrl
    Seal --> Artifact["Private Actions artifact<br/>90-day retention"]:::store
    Artifact --> Restore["Next hosted run decrypts state"]:::async
    SQLite --> Usage["Bounded usage report"]:::ctrl
    SQLite --> Diagnosis["Fixed-code diagnostic"]:::ctrl
    SQLite --> Incident["Optional temporary incident export"]:::ctrl

The state database contains run/task phases and append-only audit events. It may contain private issue text, model result metadata and bounded QA excerpts, so it is encrypted before upload. Public logs expose only safe status fields, issue numbers and aggregate timing or spend. The optional incident bundle requires a separate temporary key and is intended for one investigation, not normal runs.

Evidence surfaceWhat it provesWhat it does not prove
Project snapshotCurrent planning and ownership fieldsThat code or tests are correct
SQLite phase/event historyWhat the coordinator observed and attemptedA remote effect that was never verified
Local QA evidenceCommands and measured coverage for the candidateRequired remote CI or independent review
PR checksExact-head repository gatesProduction deployment or release acceptance
Merge verificationThe reviewed head reached mainThat a later deployment succeeded
Usage reportClaude-reported cost and elapsed timeProvider invoice accuracy

Security and failure posture#

Threat or ambiguityControl
Over-scoped GitHub tokenPreflight requires the owner, repository push access and only the allowed Project scopes
Model or QA credential leakageWorker subprocesses receive no GH_TOKEN, AUTOCD_GH_TOKEN or model key except the model process itself
Malicious issue textTrusted role prompt is separate from untrusted task data
Path escapeClaude Code working-directory restrictions, linked-worktree boundary and changed-path ownership checks
Accidental policy editUnattended auto-merge refuses .github/, .agents/, automated-cd/, AGENTS.md and other protected paths
Unknown external mutationTimeout, lost process or uncertain PR state becomes Blocked rather than replayed
Stale branch or headRemote branch and exact-head checks run before retry and merge
Budget overrunSerialized model calls receive only remaining daily allowance and unknown costs fail closed
Missing state artifactA prior execution with no approved state requires manual reconciliation

No workflow step deploys CALIBER or changes production data. Release acceptance, human approval and production operations remain in their Project Gates and operator runbooks.

Operations and recovery#

  1. Inspect the public run summary and the encrypted state artifact.
  2. Use diagnose_state=true for a bounded failure code and latest task phase.
  3. Check the live Project item, issue claim, remote branch and PR before retrying.
  4. For a pre-PR block, reconcile the branch and return the task to unassigned Todo / Ready with the required owner-authored transition comment.
  5. For a published PR, correct the same PR branch and let the next hosted tick recheck the exact head and required gates.
  6. Never reset the state database, reuse an ambiguous worktree, bypass a failed required check or claim that a Gate is complete without its evidence.

Design decisions and non-goals#

DecisionRationale
GitHub Project is authoritativePrevent a private queue from diverging from ownership, dependencies and acceptance decisions
Child Tasks, not parent Epics, are executableKeep package planning separate from implementation scope and release controls
Hosted-only executionMake credentials, audit history and merge authority visible in one remote control plane
Deterministic prefilter before model planningReduce prompt ambiguity and prevent the model from overriding policy
Isolated worktrees and worker userLimit accidental repository mutation and credential exposure
Encrypted durable stateReconcile PRs across ephemeral hosted runners without publishing private candidate content
Fail closed on uncertaintyAn unknown write, gate or cost is not evidence of success
No deployment stepKeep software engineering automation separate from release and production operations

The workflow is intentionally conservative. A daily target is a throughput objective, not a promise that six Tasks will always complete: the Project may have no Ready child Tasks, dependencies may be blocked, a model may fail, or a required remote gate may remain pending.
